method: The same objects from four advertised archives, each fetched to an empty CASC store. CDN indexes were cached. Displayed speed sampled every second, CV excludes the first five seconds. Decimal MB/s. No full client installation.
selection: before and before-repeat use the original engine. after is an intermediate round-robin candidate. after-weighted and after-final use the final host scheduling and rate estimator.
findings: Progress was emitted only after verified objects were stored. The rate window began at the first completion, omitted initial transfer time, and retained stale speed during silence.
The original engine already consumed groups in completion order. It did wait for the caller to finish storing a group before scheduling its replacement.
CASC writes were already off the network threads. Store time was about 4.2 seconds per 537 MB, so no storage-lock redesign was justified.
Only the first HTTPS mirror was used. The additional advertised hostname supported verified HTTPS but was about ten times slower in a single-range probe and sometimes disconnected.
The old throttle allowed a full read to overdraw its bucket. This was especially bursty at low limits.
Repeated live tests show no consistent throughput gain. The revised display tracks actual transfer throughput much more closely and is substantially steadier.
changes: Count socket bytes as they arrive, excluding gaps and duplicate retry progress. Emit progress during network silence.
Use an eight-second time-weighted window with a two-second warm-up. Clear rates across stages and on stop. Existing shared UI formatting derives ETA from this rate.
Choose verified HTTPS hosts by observed rate and current load. Probe unknown alternates and cool down failed hosts for 30 seconds.
Bound socket inactivity to five seconds and retry trickling responses on another host, excluding intentional throttle waits.
Schedule a replacement group before the consumer stores its predecessor, retaining bounded completion-order consumption.
Reserve bandwidth tokens before reads with a 100 ms burst allowance capped at 64 KiB. Check cancellation during reads, throttling and retry backoff.
Retain BLTE, object-size, range and index integrity checks. Checkpoint completed objects on cancellation and close CDN pools with the updater.
